entities.name: Scabies
entities.description: Contagious ectoparasitic skin infestation caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, clinically characterized by intense nocturnal pruritus, pathognomonic serpiginous intraepidermal burrows, male genital nodules, and secondary pyoderma.

entities.name: Classical Scabies
entities.description: Standard clinical syndrome of scabies presenting with a low mite burden (10-15 mites), nocturnal pruritus, and excoriated papules in classic web and flexural locations.

entities.name: Crusted Scabies
entities.description: Severe hyperkeratotic variant of scabies harboring thousands to millions of mites, with extensive scaling, crusting, and high contagiousness occurring in immunocompromised individuals.

entities.name: Nodular Scabies
entities.description: Exquisitely pruritic, firm inflammatory nodules on male genitalia, groin, or axillae representing delayed-type hypersensitivity that often persist for months following curative therapy.

entities.name: Infantile Scabies
entities.description: Atypical pediatric presentation in children under two years characterized by breakdown of adult sparing rules, involving the scalp, face, neck, palms, and soles with vesicular lesions.

entities.name: Bullous Scabies
entities.description: Rare blistering presentation of scabies mimicking bullous pemphigoid, predominantly observed in elderly patients and characterized by tense intraepidermal or subepidermal bullae.

entities.name: Scabies Incognito
entities.description: Clinically masked or atypical presentation of scabies resulting from topical or systemic corticosteroid misuse, dampening inflammation while permitting extensive mite proliferation.

entities.name: Geriatric Scabies
entities.description: Scabies presentation in elderly and bedridden individuals characterized by atypical distribution on the back, neck, and scalp, often with attenuated pruritus and high transmission risk.

entities.name: Scalp Scabies
entities.description: Cutaneous mite involvement of the scalp and hair-bearing cranial vault, typically seen in infants, bedridden elderly individuals, or patients with crusted hyperinfestation.

entities.name: Canine Scabies Transmission
entities.description: Transient, self-limiting zoonotic infestation transmitted from domestic dogs with sarcoptic mange, causing pruritic papules without epidermal burrowing or sustained human transmission.

entities.name: Impetigo
entities.description: Superficial contagious bacterial pyoderma predominantly caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes complicating excoriated scabietic skin breaches.

entities.name: Ecthyma
entities.description: Deep ulcerative cutaneous bacterial infection extending through the epidermis into the dermis, characterized by punched-out ulcers with thick hard crusts.

entities.name: Cellulitis
entities.description: Acute, spreading bacterial infection of the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissues arising from secondary inoculation through excoriated scabies lesions.

entities.name: Cutaneous Abscess
entities.description: Localized collection of purulent exudate within dermis and subcutaneous tissues resulting from pyogenic bacterial superinfection of excoriated scabietic skin.

entities.name: Furunculosis
entities.description: Painful necrotizing infection of hair follicles with purulent discharge resulting from secondary Staphylococcal superinfection of excoriated skin.

entities.name: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis
entities.description: Immune-complex mediated acute glomerulonephritis triggered by cutaneous nephritogenic Streptococcus pyogenes superinfection complicating scabies lesions.

entities.name: Acute Rheumatic Fever
entities.description: Autoimmune systemic inflammatory disease triggered by untreated Streptococcus pyogenes infections originating from cutaneous scabies pyoderma in tropical endemic areas.

entities.name: Rheumatic Heart Disease
entities.description: Chronic permanent valvular heart damage resulting from recurrent acute rheumatic fever triggered by untreated streptococcal pyoderma complicating scabies.

entities.name: Sepsis
entities.description: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host systemic response to invasive bacterial superinfection originating from excoriated scabies lesions.

entities.name: Septicemia
entities.description: Active systemic infection caused by the presence and multiplication of pyogenic bacteria in the bloodstream entering through excoriated scabietic skin breaches.

entities.name: Secondary Eczematization
entities.description: Superimposed acute or subacute eczematous dermatitis characterized by erythema, weeping, and scaling resulting from persistent scratching and epidermal barrier irritation.

entities.name: Lichenification
entities.description: Hypertrophic thickening of the epidermis with accentuated skin markings produced by repetitive mechanical rubbing and chronic excoriation in response to persistent itch.

entities.name: Excoriation Lesions
entities.description: Mechanical epidermal abrasions, gouges, and hemorrhagic crusts produced by direct fingernail scratching in response to intense scabietic pruritus.

entities.name: Post-Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation
entities.description: Acquired darkening of lesional skin sites following resolution of cutaneous inflammatory papules and excoriations, prominent in darkly pigmented individuals.

entities.name: Post-Inflammatory Hypopigmentation
entities.description: Localized loss of epidermal melanin pigment following the resolution of excoriated, superinfected, or deeply inflamed scabietic cutaneous lesions.

entities.name: Onychauxis
entities.description: Localized hypertrophy and marked thickening of nail plates with accumulated subungual hyperkeratotic mite-laden debris occurring in crusted scabies.

entities.name: Secondary Bacterial Lymphangitis
entities.description: Inflammatory bacterial infection of cutaneous lymphatic channels presenting as erythematous linear streaks spreading proximally from superinfected scabietic lesions.

entities.name: Secondary Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Reactive enlargement of regional draining lymph nodes in response to cutaneous pyogenic superinfection or severe immunological inflammation from scabies.

entities.name: Sleep Fragmentation
entities.description: Profound disruption of normal sleep architecture and chronic nocturnal insomnia directly caused by intractable nighttime exacerbation of pruritus.

entities.name: Chronic Renal Impairment
entities.description: Long-term progressive renal functional impairment resulting from cumulative glomerular damage following recurrent scabies-driven streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

entities.name: Toxic Shock Syndrome
entities.description: Severe toxin-mediated systemic illness characterized by shock, diffuse erythematous rash, and multisystem organ failure secondary to bacterial pyoderma.

entities.name: Infantile Acropustulosis
entities.description: Recurrent pruritic sterile vesicopustular eruption on the hands and feet of infants, occurring as a post-scabietic inflammatory hypersensitivity reaction.

entities.name: Scabietic Erythroderma
entities.description: Generalized, intense cutaneous erythema and exfoliative scaling involving greater than ninety percent of body surface area associated with extensive crusted scabies.

entities.name: Fissured Keratoderma
entities.description: Painful deep fissures across markedly thickened hyperkeratotic palmoplantar plaques in patients with crusted scabies, creating portals for invasive bacterial infection.

entities.name: Mite Hypersensitivity Reaction
entities.description: Type IV delayed cell-mediated immunological response to Sarcoptes scabiei antigens, saliva, and fecal scybala driving the characteristic pruritus and eruption.

entities.name: Type I Hypersensitivity
entities.description: Immediate IgE-mediated immunological response mediated by mast cell degranulation in sensitized or hyperinfested hosts, producing rapid pruritic and urticarial flares.

entities.name: Asymptomatic Primary Infestation
entities.description: Subclinical initial phase of primary infestation lasting three to six weeks during which mites tunnel and reproduce before delayed hypersensitivity triggers symptoms.

entities.name: Post-Scabietic Pruritus
entities.description: Continuation of severe itching for two to four weeks post-curative treatment caused by lingering dead mite antigens in the stratum corneum rather than active infestation.

entities.name: Recurrent Infestation
entities.description: Repeated episodes of scabies infestation occurring commonly in high-transmission environments due to the lack of sterilizing post-infestation protective immunity.

entities.name: Staphylococcal Bacteremia
entities.description: Invasive bloodstream infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus gaining entry through excoriated scabietic cutaneous lesions, predisposing to endocarditis and osteomyelitis.

entities.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
entities.description: Fulminant, life-threatening infection of subcutaneous tissue and deep fascia caused by invasive pyogenic bacteria entering through superinfected scabietic lesions.

entities.name: Interdigital Web Burrows
entities.description: Delicate sinuous intraepidermal tunnels situated in the web spaces between fingers, representing the primary pathognomonic physical finding of classical scabies.

entities.name: Flexor Wrist Burrows
entities.description: Slightly raised, thread-like intraepidermal burrows across the volar flexion creases of the wrists, serving as a highly specific diagnostic hallmark.

entities.name: Wake Sign
entities.description: V-shaped superficial epidermal scale resembling the wake of a boat located at the entrance of a scabietic burrow pointing toward the mite.

entities.name: Male Genital Nodules
entities.description: Firm, indurated, highly pruritic inflammatory nodules on the penis and scrotum of males representing a diagnostic pathognomonic hallmark.

entities.name: Glans Penis Papules
entities.description: Discrete, solid erythematous inflammatory papules on the glans penis that provide immediate high-specificity physical confirmation of scabies.

entities.name: Penile Shaft Burrows
entities.description: Elevated linear or serpiginous intraepidermal tracks on the thin cutaneous shaft of the penis harboring gravid female Sarcoptes mites.

entities.name: Female Areolar Lesions
entities.description: Excoriated inflammatory papules and eczematous changes distributed symmetrically around the areolae and inframammary creases in adolescent and adult females.

entities.name: Circle of Hebra
entities.description: Canonical topographic anatomical distribution of scabietic lesions spanning the hands, wrists, axillary folds, waistline, buttocks, and genitalia with cranial sparing.

entities.name: Anterior Axillary Papules
entities.description: Clustered excoriated inflammatory papules localized along the anterior axillary folds representing a classic topographic physical exam site.

entities.name: Periumbilical Papules
entities.description: Grouped erythematous papules and linear excoriations concentrated around the umbilicus and waistline where friction and warmth promote mite retention.

entities.name: Buttock Papules
entities.description: Bilateral crops of intensely itchy, excoriated inflammatory papules distributed across the convexities of the buttocks and inferior gluteal creases.

entities.name: Posterior Thigh Papules
entities.description: Symmetrical crops of pruritic papules and excoriations localized to the superior aspect of the posterior thighs below the gluteal fold.

entities.name: Extensor Elbow Papules
entities.description: Discrete excoriated erythematous papules clustered over the extensor aspects of the elbows and posterior olecranon regions.

entities.name: Volar Wrist Papules
entities.description: Grouped solid pruritic inflammatory papules and minute vesicles clustered on the volar flexor surfaces of the wrists.

entities.name: Ulnar Forearm Papules
entities.description: Linear or clustered crops of excoriated inflammatory papules tracking along the ulnar subcutaneous borders of the forearms.

entities.name: Malleolar Papules
entities.description: Discrete, excoriated inflammatory papules and crusted lesions clustered over the medial and lateral malleoli of the ankles.

entities.name: Palmoplantar Infantile Vesicles
entities.description: Discrete, tense fluid-filled intraepidermal vesicles located on the palms and soles of infants under two years, highly characteristic of pediatric scabies.

entities.name: Palmoplantar Infantile Pustules
entities.description: Circumscribed yellowish neutrophil-rich pustules distributed across the volar surfaces of the hands and feet in infants with scabies.

entities.name: Scalp Papules in Infants
entities.description: Diffuse inflammatory papules, crusts, and excoriations distributed across the hair-bearing scalp in infants under two years of age.

entities.name: Facial Lesions in Infants
entities.description: Excoriated papules, vesicles, and secondary crusted lesions involving the facial skin and cheeks of infants with scabies.

entities.name: Retroauricular Fold Lesions
entities.description: Macerated, excoriated inflammatory papules and fissures tucked within the retroauricular sulci in infants and young children.

entities.name: Adherent Yellow Crusts
entities.description: Massive, adherent, fissured yellow-gray hyperkeratotic crusts laden with millions of mites characteristic of crusted Norwegian scabies.

entities.name: Malodorous Cutaneous Scales
entities.description: Distinctive foul, rancid odor emanating from massive decomposing keratinaceous scales and secondary bacterial colonization in crusted scabies.

entities.name: Subungual Hyperkeratotic Debris
entities.description: Thick, chalky crumbly hyperkeratotic debris accumulating beneath nail plates in crusted scabies causing marked subungual onycholysis.

entities.name: Intense Nocturnal Pruritus
entities.description: Severe, unrelenting itching that characteristically intensifies dramatically at night, causing severe sleep disturbance and bedtime distress.

entities.name: Post-Bath Pruritus Flare
entities.description: Acute surge in generalized pruritus provoked immediately by warm water immersion or hot showers due to thermal activation of mite activity.

entities.name: Symmetrical Bilateral Distribution
entities.description: Roughly bilateral and mirror-image symmetrical distribution of inflammatory papules and excoriations across left and right body halves.

entities.name: Discrete Grouped Papules
entities.description: Clusters of three or more discrete, solid, 2 to 3 mm palpable erythematous papules located within a circumscribed anatomical zone.

entities.name: Delta-Wing Jet Sign
entities.description: Pathognomonic dermoscopic hallmark consisting of a dark pigmented triangular shape representing the anterior mite at the end of an intraepidermal burrow.

entities.name: Vapor Contrail Sign
entities.description: Curvilinear translucent whitish intraepidermal burrow track seen trailing behind the triangular mite on dermoscopy resembling an aircraft contrail.

entities.name: Handheld Dermoscopy
entities.description: Bedside optical evaluation utilizing a 10x to 20x magnification dermatoscope providing immediate non-invasive visualization of mites and burrows.

entities.name: Videodermoscopy at 200x
entities.description: High-power digital video magnification system allowing up to 200x resolution visualization of Sarcoptes scabiei internal organs, legs, and eggs in vivo.

entities.name: Reflective Confocal Microscopy
entities.description: Non-invasive in vivo optical sectioning technique providing cellular-level horizontal images of mites, eggs, and scybala within epidermal layers.

entities.name: Mineral Oil Skin Scraping
entities.description: Diagnostic skin scraping technique using a scalpel moistened with mineral oil to collect stratum corneum material for light microscopic examination.

entities.name: Adult Female Mite Visualization
entities.description: Definitive microscopic identification of the 0.3 to 0.45 mm adult female Sarcoptes scabiei ectoparasite from lesional epidermal scrapings.

entities.name: Viable Scabietic Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic identification of translucent oval-shaped parasite eggs measuring 100 to 150 micrometers within epidermal burrow scrapings.

entities.name: Scybala Identification
entities.description: Microscopic detection of characteristic small, dark brown or amber oval fecal pellets (scybala) deposited in intraepidermal tracks.

entities.name: Adhesive Tape Test
entities.description: Non-invasive diagnostic sampling method using transparent adhesive tape pressed firmly onto suspicious burrows to recover mites and eggs for microscopy.

entities.name: Burrow Ink Test
entities.description: Bedside diagnostic test where liquid ink is applied over a suspected lesion and wiped with alcohol, selectively highlighting the burrow via capillary action.

entities.name: Tetracycline Fluorescence Test
entities.description: Diagnostic bedside method utilizing topical tetracycline tracking into intraepidermal burrows, visualized as bright green-yellow fluorescence under Wood's light.

entities.name: Potassium Hydroxide Preparation
entities.description: Microscopic slide preparation utilizing 10% potassium hydroxide solution to digest keratin debris and reveal chitinous parasite structures.

entities.name: Stratum Corneum Eosinophils
entities.description: Histopathological finding on skin biopsy featuring prominent eosinophils within the stratum corneum and surrounding superficial dermal blood vessels.

entities.name: Intraepidermal Mite Burrows
entities.description: Histological cross-sectional identification of subcorneal intraepidermal tunnels containing parasite cross-sections, ova, and scybala.

entities.name: Normal Complete Blood Count
entities.description: Normal baseline complete blood count parameters with absence of leukocytosis characteristic of classical, uncomplicated scabies infestation.

entities.name: Mild Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Mild elevation of circulating peripheral blood eosinophils (5-15%) present in up to one-third of immunocompetent scabies patients.

entities.name: Marked Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Profound peripheral blood eosinophilia (>30-50%) associated with massive systemic Th2 immune activation in crusted Norwegian scabies.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated Total IgE
entities.description: Profound elevation of total serum immunoglobulin E (>1,000 to 10,000 IU/mL) characteristic of crusted hyperinfestation.

entities.name: Elevated Anti-Sarcoptes IgE
entities.description: Circulating antigen-specific immunoglobulin E directed against Sarcoptes scabiei recombinant allergen proteins indicating active immunological sensitization.

entities.name: Elevated Total Serum IgG
entities.description: Elevated circulating serum immunoglobulin G concentrations reflecting chronic intense polyclonal B-cell stimulation in severe hyperinfestation.

entities.name: Elevated Sedimentation Rate
entities.description: Nonspecific elevation in erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicating active systemic inflammation driven by secondary bacterial infection or crusted disease.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Marked elevation in circulating serum C-reactive protein acute-phase reactant signifying invasive secondary bacterial superinfection.

entities.name: Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated peripheral leukocyte count with absolute neutrophilia and bandemia indicating secondary bacterial soft tissue invasion or bacteremia.

entities.name: Elevated Anti-Streptolysin O
entities.description: Elevated serum titers of anti-streptolysin O neutralizing antibodies indicating recent antecedent exposure to Streptococcus pyogenes.

entities.name: Positive Anti-DNase B
entities.description: Elevated serum titers of anti-deoxyribonuclease B antibodies, the gold-standard serological indicator for cutaneous streptococcal pyoderma.

entities.name: Hypocomplementemia
entities.description: Markedly depressed serum complement component C3 concentration caused by alternative pathway activation in post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Detection of red blood cells on microscopic urinalysis indicating glomerular capillary inflammation from secondary streptococcal pyoderma.

entities.name: Red Blood Cell Casts
entities.description: Microscopic identification of cylindrical red blood cell casts in urinary sediment confirming active acute glomerular injury.

entities.name: Proteinuria
entities.description: Abnormal excretion of protein in the urine detected on dipstick or quantified by protein-creatinine ratio signaling glomerular barrier impairment.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Elevated serum creatinine and azotemia on renal function panels reflecting acute decline in glomerular filtration rate.

entities.name: Positive Wound Bacterial Culture
entities.description: Microbiological isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes from lesional swabs.

entities.name: Positive Blood Cultures
entities.description: Microbiological isolation of pyogenic bacterial pathogens from peripheral venipuncture blood bottles confirming systemic bacteremia.

entities.name: High-Frequency Bedside Ultrasound
entities.description: High-frequency cutaneous ultrasound (20-50 MHz) demonstrating superficial hypoechoic intraepidermal tracks and focal echogenic mite bodies.

entities.name: Optical Coherence Tomography
entities.description: Non-invasive high-resolution cross-sectional optical coherence tomography demonstrating real-time depth architecture of burrows and living mites.

entities.name: IACS Level A1 Confirmation
entities.description: Consensus criteria Level A1 confirmed scabies diagnosis requiring definitive light microscopic visualization of mites, ova, or scybala from skin scrapings.

entities.name: IACS Level A2 Confirmation
entities.description: Consensus criteria Level A2 confirmed scabies diagnosis requiring non-invasive in vivo visualization of mites or eggs using high-magnification devices.

entities.name: IACS Level A3 Confirmation
entities.description: Consensus criteria Level A3 confirmed scabies diagnosis requiring definitive visualization of the mite structure using handheld dermoscopy.

entities.name: Prolonged Skin-to-Skin Contact
entities.description: Primary transmission modality requiring continuous, direct physical cutaneous contact (typically 10-20 minutes) to transfer mites between human hosts.

entities.name: Sexual Partner Contact
entities.description: Intimate physical contact with a sexual partner facilitating efficient transfer of Sarcoptes mites across cutaneous surfaces.

entities.name: Shared Bedding and Linens
entities.description: Indirect fomite transmission route through contaminated bedsheets, blankets, and towels harboring viable mites shed from infested individuals.

entities.name: Shed Keratinaceous Crusts
entities.description: Exfoliated hyperkeratotic epidermal scales containing viable mites shed into the immediate physical environment from patients with crusted scabies.

entities.name: Overcrowded Household Environment
entities.description: High residential population density within domestic quarters promoting sustained person-to-person skin contact and repeated intra-family transmission.

entities.name: Prison Incarceration
entities.description: Correctional facility environment characterized by confinement, crowded cells, and shared physical spaces driving institutional scabies outbreaks.

entities.name: Residential Aged Care Facilities
entities.description: Long-term eldercare institutional settings where vulnerable residents and physical caregiving interactions propagate widespread scabies transmission.

entities.name: Refugee Camp Living
entities.description: Humanitarian crisis settings and displaced person encampments marked by severe shelter overcrowding and compromised sanitation promoting hypertransmission.

entities.name: Child Day-Care Centers
entities.description: Pediatric group day-care environments where close contact, communal play, and shared bedding drive pediatric transmission clusters.

entities.name: Remote Island Communities
entities.description: Isolated oceanic island and remote indigenous populations experiencing sustained high-prevalence transmission driven by communal lifestyle.

entities.name: Urban Slum Residence
entities.description: Impoverished high-density informal urban settlements lacking adequate sanitation and healthcare access, promoting continuous endemic scabies cycles.

entities.name: Primary Infection Incubation
entities.description: Asymptomatic incubation interval of three to six weeks required for a naive host to mount a Type IV hypersensitivity reaction to mite allergens.

entities.name: Reinfestation Incubation
entities.description: Rapid symptomatic incubation interval of twenty-four to forty-eight hours seen upon secondary exposure in previously sensitized hosts.

entities.name: Advanced HIV Infection
entities.description: Host condition of severe retroviral immunodeficiency characterized by CD4 lymphopenia predisposing to uninhibited parasite proliferation and crusted scabies.

entities.name: HTLV-1 Coinfection
entities.description: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 infection causing profound cutaneous immune dysregulation and exceptional susceptibility to crusted scabies.

entities.name: Solid Organ Transplantation
entities.description: Post-transplant host state requiring lifelong pharmacological immunosuppression that severely impairs cutaneous cell-mediated parasite clearance.

entities.name: Chronic Corticosteroid Therapy
entities.description: Pharmacological host immunosuppression induced by prolonged systemic or high-potency topical glucocorticoids suppressing anti-mite immunity.

entities.name: Down Syndrome
entities.description: Genetic condition characterized by trisomy 21 with associated cutaneous immune alterations predisposing to hyperkeratotic crusted scabies.

entities.name: Severe Dementia
entities.description: Profound neurocognitive impairment preventing patients from verbalizing pruritus or executing mechanical scratching responses to control parasite burden.

entities.name: Bedridden Debilitated Patients
entities.description: Severely physically disabled and bedridden individuals unable to perform physical scratching, bathing, or grooming to limit parasite loads.

entities.name: Pediatric Age Under 2
entities.description: Infants and children under twenty-four months of age possessing delicate epidermal architecture and immature cellular immunity promoting atypical dissemination.

entities.name: Elderly Care Residents
entities.description: Geriatric residents of communal long-term care facilities characterized by age-associated immunosenescence and dependency on hands-on caregiving.

entities.name: Household Cluster Itch
entities.description: Epidemiological exposure history of simultaneous or sequential nocturnal pruritus and matching skin eruptions among co-habiting domestic contacts.

entities.name: Total Absence of Pruritus
entities.description: Complete absence of cutaneous pruritus or scratching behavior in an alert, immunocompetent host strongly ruling out classical scabies.

entities.name: Adult Facial Involvement
entities.description: Presence of primary pruritic cutaneous papules across the face, cheeks, and scalp in an immunocompetent adult contradicting the adult cephalic sparing rule.

entities.name: Sparing of Finger Webs
entities.description: Complete physical sparing of interdigital web spaces of both hands in a patient presenting with widespread pruritic papules.

entities.name: Sparing of Flexor Wrists
entities.description: Total absence of burrows, papules, or excoriations across the volar aspects and flexor creases of both wrists.

entities.name: High Fever at Onset
entities.description: Acute high-grade fever and rigors at initial presentation without clinical evidence of secondary pyogenic bacterial soft tissue infection.

entities.name: Systemic Toxicity at Onset
entities.description: Presence of hemodynamic instability, marked prostration, or acute toxic encephalopathy at initial hospital presentation.

entities.name: Non-Pruritic Palmoplantar Macules
entities.description: Painless, completely non-pruritic copper-red or violaceous maculopapular lesions on the palms and soles characteristic of secondary syphilis.

entities.name: Isolated Extensor Plaque Sparing
entities.description: Hyperkeratotic scaly plaques restricted strictly to extensor knees and elbows with complete sparing of flexural surfaces and interdigital webs.

entities.name: Auspitz Sign Positivity
entities.description: Elicitation of pinpoint capillary bleeding upon mechanical removal of dry silvery epidermal scales characteristic of plaque psoriasis.

entities.name: Exclusive Sun-Exposed Distribution
entities.description: Cutaneous eruption strictly demarcated to photo-exposed body regions with sharp cutoff at clothing margins.

entities.name: Pure Mucosal Ulceration
entities.description: Ulcerative erosions restricted entirely to mucous membranes lacking a keratinized stratum corneum (oral cavity, vaginal mucosa).

entities.name: Targetoid Iris Lesions
entities.description: Concentric three-zone target lesions with dark central blister or crust surrounded by pale edema and peripheral erythematous halo.

entities.name: Flaccid Bullae with Nikolsky
entities.description: Fragile, easily ruptured flaccid blisters with lateral epidermal sloughing under mechanical shearing pressure confirming pemphigus.

entities.name: Rapid Day-One Rash Resolution
entities.description: Spontaneous, complete vanishing of individual cutaneous pruritic lesions within twenty-four hours without scabicidal intervention.

entities.name: Lack of Household Itch
entities.description: Multi-year chronic intractable pruritus in an adult with confirmed complete absence of itch or rash in co-sleeping bed partners.

entities.name: Normal Serum IgE Norwegian
entities.description: Normal total serum IgE level and normal absolute eosinophil count in an extensively crusted erythrodermic patient excluding Norwegian scabies.

entities.name: Ceftriaxone Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Complete, permanent resolution of pruritus and cutaneous rash following beta-lactam antibacterial therapy alone without scabicides.

entities.name: Burrow and Mite Absence
entities.description: Repeated negative expert high-resolution dermoscopic surveys and serial mineral oil skin scrapings across all candidate cutaneous sites.

entities.name: Wheals Resolving Under 24h
entities.description: Transient, migratory, pruritic edematous erythematous plaques that completely resolve within twenty-four hours without epidermal changes.

entities.name: Exclusive Scalp Folliculitis
entities.description: Pustular and inflammatory lesions strictly centered around cranial hair follicles on the scalp without trunk or extremity lesions.

entities.name: Unilateral Dermatomal Vesicles
entities.description: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base strictly respecting the anatomical boundaries of a single unilateral sensory dermatome.

entities.name: Petechial Non-Blanching Purpura
entities.description: Non-blanching erythematous or violaceous macules and palpable purpura caused by erythrocyte extravasation indicating cutaneous vasculitis.

entities.name: Atopic Dermatitis
entities.description: Chronic pruritic inflammatory skin disease characterized by xerosis, flexural lichenified plaques, personal or family history of atopy, and absence of linear burrows or contagious household spread.

entities.name: Bullous Pemphigoid
entities.description: Autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease of the elderly mediated by autoantibodies against BP180 and BP230, producing tense bullae and linear basement membrane zone immunoreactants.

entities.name: Insect Bites
entities.description: Cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction to arthropod bites presenting as grouped pruritic erythematous papules or wheals on exposed skin areas with a central punctum.

entities.name: Plaque Psoriasis
entities.description: Chronic autoimmune papulosquamous disorder characterized by sharply circumscribed erythematous plaques with silvery-white micaceous scales on extensor surfaces and absence of ectoparasites.

entities.name: Secondary Syphilis
entities.description: Systemic spirochetal infection caused by Treponema pallidum presenting with a non-pruritic copper-red maculopapular rash involving palms and soles, lymphadenopathy, and positive serology.

entities.name: Papular Urticaria
entities.description: Recurrent, hypersensitivity-driven cutaneous eruption in young children presenting with crops of pruritic papulovesicles and urticarial lesions following sporadic arthropod bites.

entities.name: Folliculitis
entities.description: Localized superficial inflammation or infection of hair follicles manifesting as discrete pustules centered on hair shafts without intraepidermal linear tunneling.

entities.name: Contact Dermatitis
entities.description: Inflammatory cutaneous reaction triggered by direct contact with exogenous irritants or allergens, exhibiting sharp borders reflecting contact distribution.

entities.name: Seborrheic Dermatitis
entities.description: Common chronic superficial dermatosis characterized by greasy, yellowish scaling and erythema on areas with high sebaceous gland concentration, sparing classic scabies sites.

entities.name: Darier Disease
entities.description: Autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by greasy, malodorous hyperkeratotic papules in seborrheic areas, characteristic nail changes, and suprabasal acantholysis.

entities.name: Dermatitis Herpetiformis
entities.description: Intensely pruritic, autoimmune blistering cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease presenting with symmetrical grouped excoriated vesicles on extensor surfaces and granular IgA deposition.

entities.name: Pityriasis Rosea
entities.description: Acute, self-limiting papulosquamous eruption characterized by a solitary herald patch followed by oval scaly plaques oriented along skin cleavage lines in a Christmas-tree distribution.

entities.name: Cutaneous Larva Migrans
entities.description: Zoonotic hookworm nematode larvae migration producing rapidly advancing, intensely pruritic serpiginous cutaneous tracks on lower extremities following contaminated sand contact.

entities.name: Delusional Parasitosis
entities.description: Monothematic psychiatric disorder characterized by a fixed, unshakeable delusion of skin parasite infestation accompanied by neurotic excoriations and negative objective physical findings.

entities.name: Dyshidrotic Eczema
entities.description: Recurrent vesicular dermatosis characterized by deep-seated, pruritic tapioca pudding-like vesicles localized to the lateral digits, palms, and plantar surfaces.

entities.name: Lichen Planus
entities.description: Chronic inflammatory mucocutaneous disorder presenting with polygonal, violaceous, flat-topped pruritic papules with Wickham striae on flexor wrists and frequent oral mucosal involvement.

entities.name: Varicella Zoster Virus
