relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, classical scabies, ordinary scabies, low mite burden, typical presentation
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as classical scabies, the standard presentation characterized by a low parasite burden of 10 to 15 adult female mites, presenting with widespread excoriated papules, serpiginous burrows, and severe nocturnal pruritus.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, crusted scabies, Norwegian scabies, hyperinfestation, hyperkeratotic plaques
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as crusted scabies (Norwegian scabies), a severe hyperinfestation syndrome occurring in immunocompromised or debilitated hosts characterized by millions of mites, massive adherent hyperkeratotic crusts, and often reduced or absent pruritus.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, nodular scabies, pruritic nodules, delayed hypersensitivity, persistent lesions
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as nodular scabies, characterized by persistent, intensely pruritic, firm reddish-brown inflammatory nodules on the male genitalia, axillae, and groin that represent hypersensitivity and may persist months after parasite eradication.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, infantile scabies, pediatric presentation, diffuse involvement, palmoplantar vesicles
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as infantile scabies in children under two years of age, presenting atypically with diffuse involvement of the scalp, face, neck, palms, and soles, often featuring vesicles, pustules, and sleep disruption.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, bullous scabies, blistering eruption, pemphigoid mimic, tense bullae
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as bullous scabies, an uncommon atypical variant primarily affecting elderly patients characterized by tense fluid-filled subepidermal bullae that closely mimics bullous pemphigoid.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, scabies incognito, corticosteroid modification, masked presentation, atypical morphology
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as scabies incognito following topical or systemic corticosteroid therapy, where local immunosuppression dampens inflammatory erythema and pruritus while masking classic burrows and promoting widespread mite proliferation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, geriatric scabies, elderly presentation, nursing home outbreak, atypical distribution
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as geriatric scabies in elderly institutionalized individuals, often presenting with subtle or atypical lesions on the back, pressure points, and scalp, accompanied by diminished pruritic awareness due to cognitive impairment.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, scalp scabies, cranial involvement, pediatric and crusted variants, follicular scaling
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as scalp scabies in neonates, young infants, and patients with crusted scabies, producing scaling, papules, crusts, and alopecia on the scalp and retroauricular areas.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, canine scabies, Sarcoptes scabiei var canis, animal contact, self-limiting papules
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as canine scabies transmission (sarcoptic mange cross-infestation) when Sarcoptes scabiei var. canis temporarily infests humans from pets, causing transient excoriated papules without burrowing or sustained reproduction.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, secondary impetigo, pyoderma, honey-colored crusts, superficial bacterial superinfection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as secondary impetigo when epidermal barrier disruption from mite burrowing and intense excoriation allows superficial bacterial superinfection by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes, producing honey-colored crusts.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, ecthyma, ulcerative pyoderma, deep bacterial infection, streptococcal invasion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as ecthyma, a deep ulcerative bacterial superinfection penetrating through the epidermis into the dermis with adherent thick hard crusts, commonly complicating chronic excoriated lesions in tropical climates.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, cellulitis, deep soft tissue infection, spreading erythema, bacterial invasion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as cellulitis when secondary bacterial pathogens (Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) invade deeper subcutaneous tissues through excoriation tracks, resulting in spreading cutaneous erythema, warmth, and systemic toxicity.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, cutaneous abscess, subcutaneous pus collection, staphylococcal superinfection, fluctuance
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as cutaneous abscess formation, where pyogenic bacteria inoculated via pruritic scratching form localized collections of purulent exudate within the dermis and deeper subcutaneous tissue.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, furunculosis, infected hair follicles, boils, staphylococcal superinfection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as furunculosis when secondary Staphylococcus aureus superinfection tracks into adjacent hair follicles, producing painful necrotizing follicular nodules and boils.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, PSGN, immune-complex nephropathy, nephritic syndrome
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN), an immune-complex mediated renal disease triggered by secondary Streptococcus pyogenes impetigo on excoriated skin, leading to hematuria, hypertension, and edema.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, acute rheumatic fever, ARF, streptococcal sequela, autoimmune carditis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as acute rheumatic fever (ARF) in endemic populations, where secondary cutaneous Streptococcus pyogenes pyoderma drives autoimmune systemic inflammation targeting cardiac tissue, joints, and central nervous system.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, rheumatic heart disease, RHD, chronic valvulopathy, post-streptococcal damage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as chronic rheumatic heart disease (RHD) as a long-term consequence of recurrent episodes of scabies-driven streptococcal pyoderma and repetitive acute rheumatic fever, leading to permanent cardiac valvular damage.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, sepsis, life-threatening organ dysfunction, bacteremia, invasive infection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as sepsis, a life-threatening systemic organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host responses following invasive bacterial entry (Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) via disrupted skin barriers.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, septicemia, bacterial bloodstream invasion, bacteremia, pyogenic dissemination
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as septicemia when severe secondary pyoderma and excoriated ulcerations allow direct entry of pyogenic pathogens into the bloodstream, creating overt bacteremia and septic shock risk.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, secondary eczematization, autosensitization, pruritic plaques, spongiotic dermatitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as secondary eczematization, where chronic scratching and immune sensitization to mite components provoke widespread spongiotic erythematous, weeping, or scaling eczematous plaques.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, lichenification, skin thickening, exaggerated markings, chronic scratching
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as lichenification, presenting as localized or generalized thickening of the epidermis with exaggerated skin markings resulting from unrelenting chronic mechanical rubbing and scratching.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, excoriations, linear scratch marks, epidermal loss, trauma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as excoriation lesions, presenting as punctate or linear epidermal abrasions, hemorrhagic crusts, and gouged skin tracks produced by vigorous fingernail scratching.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, PIH, dark macules, resolving lesions
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, characterized by persistent dark brown or slate-gray macules remaining at sites of healed burrows, papules, and excoriations, especially in darker skin types.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, depigmented macules, post-scabietic healing
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, presenting as pale or depigmented macules and patches following resolution of severe excoriated or superinfected scabietic lesions.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, onychauxis, subungual hyperkeratosis, thickened dystrophic nails, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as onychauxis (subungual hyperkeratosis and nail dystrophy) in crusted scabies, where mites invade the nail bed and matrix, causing massive thickening, crumbly debris, and nail plate distortion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, secondary lymphangitis, erythematous streaks, lymphatic spread, bacterial infection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as secondary bacterial lymphangitis, presenting with tender erythematous linear streaking extending proximally along lymphatic channels from superinfected excoriated skin lesions.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, secondary lymphadenopathy, reactive lymphadenitis, enlarged nodes, regional drainage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as secondary lymphadenopathy, characterized by tender enlargement of regional draining lymph nodes (axillary, epitrochlear, inguinal) responding to secondary bacterial pyoderma and severe cutaneous inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, sleep fragmentation, nocturnal insomnia, impaired quality of life, severe itch
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as severe sleep fragmentation and nocturnal insomnia resulting from unremitting nocturnal exacerbation of pruritus, leading to exhaustion, cognitive impairment, and school or work absenteeism.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, chronic renal impairment, long-term nephropathy, glomerular scarring, persistent hematuria
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as chronic renal impairment in resource-poor endemic settings where recurrent episodes of scabies-associated post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis result in cumulative glomerular damage, proteinuria, and renal decline.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, toxic shock syndrome, TSS, exotoxin-mediated illness, hemodynamic collapse
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as toxic shock syndrome when superinfecting Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes strains release pyrogenic exotoxins through extensive skin breaches, causing fever, hypotension, and multiorgan failure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, infantile acropustulosis, post-scabietic pustules, palmoplantar vesicles, hypersensitivity
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as infantile acropustulosis, presenting as recurring intensely pruritic sterile vesicopustules on the palms and soles of infants, representing a post-infectious hypersensitivity reaction that can recur for months.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, scabietic erythroderma, red man syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, widespread scaling
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as scabietic erythroderma in severe crusted scabies, presenting with generalized exfoliative erythema and scaling involving over 90% of total body surface area, accompanied by thermoregulatory disturbance.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, fissured keratoderma, painful cracks, thick palmoplantar plaques, crusted variant
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as fissured keratoderma in advanced crusted scabies, where hyperkeratotic plaque accumulation on the palms and soles produces deep, painful, bleeding fissures that compromise mobility and invite deep bacterial invasion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, mite hypersensitivity, Type IV reaction, delayed hypersensitivity, pruritic rash
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as a systemic mite hypersensitivity reaction, where cell-mediated Type IV delayed immunological responses to mite saliva, eggs, and fecal scybala produce generalized pruritus and widespread polymorphic cutaneous lesions.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, type I hypersensitivity, IgE-mediated response, immediate wheals, urticarial flare
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as type I immediate hypersensitivity in re-infested or crusted scabies hosts, where elevated parasite-specific IgE and mast cell degranulation trigger immediate urticarial whealing and explosive pruritus.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, asymptomatic primary infestation, subclinical phase, silent carriage, delayed allergy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as an asymptomatic primary infestation during the initial 3 to 6 weeks following first inoculation, where burrowing mites reproduce subclinically prior to host immunological sensitization.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, post-scabietic pruritus, persistent post-treatment itch, dead mite antigens, benign course
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as post-scabietic pruritus, a benign self-limiting continuation of severe itching lasting 2 to 4 weeks after successful parasitological cure caused by delayed clearance of dead mite carcasses and antigens from the stratum corneum.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, recurrent infestation, repeated infection, absence of immunity, endemic persistence
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as recurrent infestation in endemic regions because previous infestation confers incomplete protective immunity, permitting rapid clinical relapse within 24 to 48 hours upon re-exposure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, staphylococcal bacteremia, S aureus bloodstream infection, systemic pyoderma, seeding
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as Staphylococcal bacteremia when secondary Staphylococcus aureus colonization of excoriated lesions penetrates into dermal capillaries, causing bloodstream dissemination and metastatic seeding.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, necrotizing fasciitis, fulminant soft tissue necrosis, flesh-eating infection, streptococcal invasion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Scabies manifests as necrotizing fasciitis in rare severe instances when invasive Group A Streptococcus or polymicrobial flora penetrate deep fascial planes beneath chronic excoriated or crusted scabies lesions.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, interdigital burrows, web spaces, pathognomonic tracks, intraepidermal tunnels
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays pathognomonic interdigital web burrows, presenting as delicate, thread-like, sinuous or linear intraepidermal tracks (1 to 10 mm in length) across the finger web spaces harboring the gravid female mite.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, flexor wrist burrows, volar wrist, pathognomonic tunnels, epidermal tracks
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays flexor wrist burrows, appearing as slightly raised, silvery-gray or brownish wavy tracks located across the volar skin folds of the wrists, providing definitive bedside clinical confirmation.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, wake sign, V-shaped scale, burrow entrance, pathognomonic sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays the pathognomonic wake sign, characterized by a distinct V-shaped triangular epidermal scale at the point of burrow entry pointing opposite to the forward tunneling direction of the adult female mite.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, male genital nodules, penile nodules, scrotal nodules, pathognomonic sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays male genital nodules, presenting as firm, indurated, exquisitely pruritic reddish-brown or violaceous inflammatory nodules on the penile shaft, corona, glans, prepuce, and scrotum (2020 IACS Level B2).

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, glans penis papules, genital scabies, pathognomonic lesions, male examination
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays glans penis papules, presenting as discrete, solid, highly pruritic erythematous inflammatory papules on the glans that provide immediate high-specificity diagnostic evidence in male patients.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, penile shaft burrows, genital tunneling, pathognomonic intraepidermal tracks, male exam
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Scabies displays penile shaft burrows, presenting as elevated linear or tortuous epidermal tracks along the thin skin of the penile shaft terminating in a tiny papulovesicle containing a female mite.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, areolar lesions, nipple eczema, breast involvement, female predilection
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits female areolar lesions, presenting as intensely pruritic excoriated papules, crusted erosions, and eczematous changes localized symmetrically around the nipples, areolae, and inframammary folds.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, Circle of Hebra, classic distribution, topographic predilection, sparing head
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits the classic Circle of Hebra distribution, an anatomical predilection pattern involving finger webs, wrists, axillae, periumbilical abdomen, buttocks, and genitalia while strictly sparing the adult face and scalp.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, anterior axillary papules, axillary folds, inflammatory clusters, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits anterior axillary papules, presenting as discrete, clustered, excoriated erythematous inflammatory papules situated within and along the borders of the anterior axillary folds.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, periumbilical papules, waistline lesions, beltline distribution, excoriated papules
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits periumbilical papules, presenting as densely grouped excoriated papules and crusted scratch marks circling the umbilicus and extending horizontally along the waistline and beltline.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, buttock papules, gluteal fold, inferior gluteal lesions, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits buttock papules, presenting as bilateral crops of discrete, firm, excoriated erythematous papules concentrated over the buttocks and inferior gluteal folds.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, posterior thigh papules, upper thighs, grouped lesions, physical finding
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits posterior thigh papules, appearing as symmetrically distributed crops of pruriginous papules on the upper posterior thighs extending immediately below the gluteal sulcus.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, extensor elbow papules, olecranon area, excoriated lesions, physical finding
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits extensor elbow papules, presenting as scattered, crusted inflammatory papules located over the extensor surface of the elbows and olecranon prominences.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, volar wrist papules, flexor wrist, typical lesions, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits volar wrist papules, presenting as groups of 2 to 3 mm solid, highly itchy erythematous papules and small vesicles situated directly on the flexor aspects of both wrists.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, ulnar forearm papules, forearm border, linear distribution, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits ulnar forearm papules, presenting as linear arrays or crops of excoriated inflammatory papules tracking along the medial and ulnar margins of the forearms.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, malleolar papules, ankle lesions, perimalleolar eruption, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits malleolar papules, appearing as excoriated, firm pruritic papules and occasional burrows clustered around the medial and lateral malleoli and dorsum of the feet.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, palmoplantar infantile vesicles, pediatric blisters, palm and sole vesicles, infantile sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits palmoplantar infantile vesicles, presenting as clear, tense, discrete fluid-filled blisters on the palms and soles of infants under two years of age, reflecting immature skin barrier architecture.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, palmoplantar infantile pustules, acropustules, pediatric pustules, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits palmoplantar infantile pustules, presenting as small circumscribed yellowish pustules filled with neutrophils situated on the soles and palms of young children.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, scalp papules in infants, pediatric scalp rash, cranial involvement, infantile breakdown
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits scalp papules in infants, demonstrating breakdown of the adult sparing rule with diffuse inflammatory papules, scales, and crusts across the hair-bearing scalp and vertex.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, facial lesions in infants, pediatric facial rash, cheeks and chin, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits facial lesions in infants, presenting with discrete excoriated papulovesicles and crusted eczematous lesions over the cheeks, chin, and perioral skin.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, retroauricular fold lesions, behind ears, infant folds, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits retroauricular fold lesions, presenting as macerated, excoriated, erythematous papules and linear fissures tucked directly within the skin creases behind the ears in infants.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, adherent yellow crusts, Norwegian crusts, hyperkeratosis, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits adherent yellow crusts in crusted (Norwegian) scabies, presenting as massive, thick, fissured, yellow-gray or brownish hyperkeratotic scales adhering tenaciously to hands, feet, and pressure points.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, malodorous cutaneous scales, foul odor, crusted scabies, keratin debris
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits malodorous cutaneous scales in advanced crusted presentations, where massive accumulation of decomposing desquamated keratin, mite feces, and secondary bacterial colonies emit a foul, rancid odor.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, subungual hyperkeratotic debris, nail dystrophy, crumbly nails, crusted sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits subungual hyperkeratotic debris, presenting with thick, chalky, yellowish-white crumbly crusts accumulating under fingernails and toenails, elevating and splitting the dystrophic nail plates.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, intense nocturnal pruritus, severe night itching, sleep disturbance, primary hallmark
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits intense nocturnal pruritus, a hallmark clinical symptom characterized by severe, unrelenting itching that worsens dramatically at night and awakens patients from deep sleep.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, post-bath pruritus flare, warm water itching, thermal exacerbation, physical hallmark
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits a post-bath pruritus flare, characterized by an acute, distressing surge in generalized cutaneous itch triggered immediately following warm baths or hot showers due to increased skin perfusion and mite motility.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, symmetrical bilateral distribution, mirror lesions, systemic hypersensitivity, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits symmetrical bilateral distribution, where inflammatory papules and excoriations appear in roughly mirror-image patterns across the left and right sides of the body due to systemic hypersensitivity.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, discrete grouped papules, clustered lesions, typical morphology, physical sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scabies exhibits discrete grouped papules, defined by clusters of three or more small (2 to 3 mm), solid, easily palpable erythematous inflammatory papules situated within an anatomical area of 10 to 20 cm.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, delta-wing jet sign, dermoscopy hallmark, triangular mite head, hang-glider sign
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates the pathognomonic delta-wing jet sign on dermoscopy, characterized by a dark, pigmented triangular structure (representing the pigmented head, anterior body, and first two pairs of legs of the female mite) situated at the burrow terminus.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, vapor contrail sign, burrow track, dermoscopy, translucent wavy trail
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates the vapor contrail sign on dermoscopy, represented by the whitish, translucent, curvilinear epidermal tunnel trailing behind the delta-wing mite head, completing the appearance of a jet with a condensation contrail.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, handheld dermoscopy, bedside examination, 10x-20x magnification, non-invasive triage
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates high diagnostic yield on handheld dermoscopy at 10x to 20x magnification, enabling immediate non-invasive bedside triage and visualization of burrows and living mites within minutes.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, videodermoscopy at 200x, high magnification, anatomical visualization, mite gut and legs
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates detailed anatomical structures on videodermoscopy at 200x magnification, revealing the translucent oval body, peristaltic gut movements, anterior bristles, and laid eggs within the burrow.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, reflective confocal microscopy, RCM, cellular sectioning, in vivo optical biopsy
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates in vivo cellular detail on reflective confocal microscopy (RCM), displaying real-time horizontal optical sections of the oval mite body (0.3 mm) in the upper stratum spinosum with surrounding hyperkeratosis and fecal scybala.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, mineral oil skin scraping, scalpel scraping, light microscopy, classic diagnostic test
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits definitive parasitological confirmation on mineral oil skin scraping, where superficial epidermal scalpel scrapings of unexcoriated burrows mounted on a glass slide demonstrate mites under light microscopy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, adult female mite visualization, 0.4 mm ectoparasite, eight-legged arachnid, diagnostic hallmark
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits direct adult female mite visualization on optical microscopy, identifying the 0.3 to 0.45 mm oval, dorsoventrally flattened, tortoise-like arachnid equipped with four pairs of short legs and dorsal spines.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, viable scabietic eggs, translucent oval ova, 100-150 um, microscopic confirmation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits viable scabietic eggs on microscopic examination, presenting as smooth, translucent, oval-shaped structures measuring 100 to 150 micrometers in length containing developing larvae.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, scybala identification, fecal pellets, dark brown ovals, diagnostic waste
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits scybala identification on microscopy, demonstrating numerous small (15 to 30 micrometer), dark brown or black oval fecal pellets deposited within epidermal burrows by feeding mites.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, adhesive tape test, cellophane strip test, non-invasive sampling, pediatric collection
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits diagnostic utility with the adhesive tape test, where transparent cellophane tape firmly pressed against suspicious burrows and peeled off captures superficial stratum corneum containing mites for direct slide examination.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, burrow ink test, BIT, surgical marker ink, capillary tracking, bedside sign
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits positive burrow ink test (BIT), where applying dark ink or a surgical skin marker over a lesion and wiping away excess with alcohol leaves a sharp, dark zig-zag line tracking through the burrow canal.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, tetracycline fluorescence test, Wood's lamp, fluorescent burrow, ultraviolet exam
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits positive tetracycline fluorescence test, where topical tetracycline ointment applied to lesional skin tracks into burrows and fluoresces bright yellow-green under Wood's lamp ultraviolet illumination.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, potassium hydroxide preparation, 10 percent KOH mount, keratinolysis, microscopy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits clear microscopic resolution on potassium hydroxide (10% KOH) preparation, where gentle alkali digestion dissolves thick background keratinocytes while preserving chitinous mite exoskeletons and egg casings.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, stratum corneum eosinophils, superficial perivascular infiltrate, dermal infiltrate, biopsy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits stratum corneum eosinophils and a dense superficial and deep perivascular dermal infiltrate rich in eosinophils and histiocytes on punch biopsy of inflammatory papules and nodules.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, intraepidermal mite burrows, histology sections, subcorneal tunnel, chitinous fragments
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits intraepidermal mite burrows on histopathology, showing horizontal tunneling confined strictly within the cornified layer with preserved mite body parts, pincer mouthparts, and pink-staining egg shells.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, normal complete blood count, normal CBC, uncomplicated scabies, baseline labs
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies typically exhibits a normal complete blood count (CBC) in classical uncomplicated presentations, with leukocyte, hemoglobin, and platelet counts remaining well within normal physiological reference ranges.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, mild peripheral eosinophilia, 5 to 15 percent eosinophils, allergic response, blood count
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits mild peripheral eosinophilia (5% to 15% of total white blood cell count) in approximately 20% to 30% of classical presentations reflecting systemic allergic hypersensitivity to mite antigens.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, marked peripheral eosinophilia, profound eosinophilia, greater than 30 percent, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits marked peripheral eosinophilia (>30% to 50% differential or absolute counts >3,000/uL) characteristically in patients presenting with crusted (Norwegian) scabies.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, markedly elevated total IgE, hyperimmunoglobulinemia E, extreme IgE, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits markedly elevated total serum IgE levels (frequently exceeding 1,000 to 10,000 IU/mL) in patients with crusted hyperinfestation, reflecting massive polyclonal B-cell activation driven by Th2 cytokines.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated anti-Sarcoptes IgE, specific antibodies, parasite IgE, serological marker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits elevated specific anti-Sarcoptes IgE antibodies in circulating serum, demonstrating active immunological sensitization against recombinant mite antigens such as Sar s 1 and Sar s 14.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated total serum IgG, hypergammaglobulinemia, humoral response, crusted scabies
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits elevated total serum IgG levels with hypergammaglobulinemia in severe crusted scabies, driven by prolonged antigen exposure and chronic cutaneous immune stimulation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated sedimentation rate, elevated ESR, inflammatory marker, pyoderma complication
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR > 30 to 60 mm/hr) when complicated by secondary bacterial pyoderma, impetigo, or severe widespread crusted erythroderma.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated C-reactive protein, high CRP, acute phase reactant, bacterial superinfection
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits elevated C-reactive protein (CRP > 50 to 100 mg/L) at triage admission when secondary bacterial superinfections (cellulitis, abscess, or invasive pyoderma) complicate the skin infestation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, neutrophilic leukocytosis, left shift, high WBC, bacterial pyoderma complication
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 12,000 to 20,000/uL with bandemia > 10%) on complete blood count when complicated by invasive Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes soft tissue infections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated anti-streptolysin O, high ASO titer, streptococcal serology, post-pyoderma marker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits elevated anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titers in serum following secondary Streptococcus pyogenes impetiginization, providing serological evidence of recent streptococcal infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, positive anti-DNase B, high anti-DNase B, cutaneous streptococcal marker, pyoderma confirmation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits positive anti-DNase B antibody titers, the most reliable and sensitive serological marker for confirming preceding cutaneous Streptococcus pyogenes pyoderma triggering post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hypocomplementemia, low C3 complement, immune complex consumption, PSGN marker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits hypocomplementemia with selectively depressed serum C3 levels during admission triage in patients developing post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis secondary to scabietic impetigo.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, microscopic hematuria, dysmorphic red cells, urinalysis triage, post-streptococcal nephritis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits microscopic hematuria on admission urinalysis triage in up to 10% of children in endemic settings, signaling subclinical or overt acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis from secondary streptococcal pyoderma.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, red blood cell casts, RBC casts, dysmorphic urinary casts, glomerulonephritis hallmark
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits urinary red blood cell casts on urine sediment microscopy in patients presenting with scabies-induced acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, definitively localizing bleeding to the renal glomerulus.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, proteinuria, urinary protein, dipstick protein, glomerular breach
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits proteinuria on dipstick urinalysis and spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio during triage evaluation of post-streptococcal renal sequelae triggered by secondary impetigo.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated serum creatinine, acute kidney injury, renal dysfunction, PSGN azotemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen on admission chemistry panels in patients experiencing acute kidney injury secondary to post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, positive wound bacterial culture, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, purulent swab
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits positive wound bacterial cultures yielding heavy growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Strep) from swabs of excoriated, weeping, or honey-crusted lesions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, positive blood cultures, bacteremia, bloodstream pathogen isolation, sepsis triage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies exhibits positive blood cultures demonstrating invasive Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes in febrile hospitalized patients with secondary septicemia originating from skin breaches.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, high-frequency bedside ultrasound, HFUS, 20-50 MHz probe, epidermal imaging
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates subcorneal hypoechoic linear channels and an echogenic focal shadow with an acoustic wake on 20 to 50 MHz high-frequency bedside ultrasound (HFUS), non-invasively detecting the mite in real time.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, optical coherence tomography, OCT, cross-sectional imaging, non-invasive optical scan
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies demonstrates optical coherence tomography (OCT) cross-sectional imaging of the epidermis showing a clearly demarcated, round-to-oval reflective structure (the mite body) nestled within a subcorneal tunnel.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, IACS Level A1 confirmation, microscopy confirmation, 2020 consensus, definitive diagnosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Scabies fulfills 2020 IACS Level A1 confirmed diagnosis when light microscopic examination of skin scrapings definitively identifies adult mites, immature nymphal stages, viable eggs, or fecal scybala.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, IACS Level A2 confirmation, high-magnification device, videodermoscopy, confocal microscopy
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies fulfills 2020 IACS Level A2 confirmed diagnosis when high-magnification in vivo imaging devices (videodermoscopy >= 70x or reflectance confocal microscopy) definitively visualize living mites or eggs in intact skin.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, IACS Level A3 confirmation, dermoscopy confirmation, delta-wing sign, clinical certainty
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Scabies fulfills 2020 IACS Level A3 confirmed diagnosis when standard dermoscopy (10x-20x) definitively visualizes the diagnostic triangular head and anterior legs of the mite (delta-wing sign) at a burrow end.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, prolonged skin contact, direct transmission, 10 to 20 minutes, holding hands
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies is transmitted via direct prolonged skin-to-skin contact, typically requiring 10 to 20 minutes of continuous physical contact (such as holding hands or co-sleeping) to transfer slow-moving adult female mites in classical scabies.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, sexual partner contact, sexually transmitted infestation, intimate exposure, partner transfer
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies is transmitted through sexual partner contact, functioning as a sexually transmitted ectoparasitic infestation in sexually active young adults where prolonged intimate body contact facilitates efficient mite transfer.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, shared bedding and linens, fomite transmission, indirect contact, crusted contamination
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission occurs via shared bedding and linens, representing an important indirect fomite pathway primarily in patients with crusted scabies who shed millions of viable mites onto bedsheets and towels.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, shed keratinaceous crusts, environmental dust, exfoliated scales, crusted transmission
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission occurs via shed keratinaceous crusts in institutional environments harboring patients with Norwegian scabies, where desiccated epidermal scales in room dust retain viable mites for 48 to 72 hours.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, overcrowded household environment, domestic crowding, close quarters, transmission amplifier
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission is amplified within an overcrowded household environment, where high domestic density, shared sleeping arrangements, and multi-generational co-sleeping facilitate continuous cycle transmission.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, prison incarceration, correctional facilities, institutional outbreak, crowded cells
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission occurs readily during prison incarceration, where confined living quarters, high inmate turnover, shared bunks, and delayed medical recognition create explosive institutional outbreaks.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, residential aged care facilities, nursing homes, eldercare institutions, nosocomial outbreaks
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies outbreaks are hyperendemic in residential aged care facilities, where bedridden residents, frequent hands-on nursing care, and undiagnosed crusted scabies index cases cause prolonged nosocomial spread.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, refugee camp living, displaced persons, humanitarian crises, crowded tents
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission is heavily driven by refugee camp living and displaced person settlements, where extreme overcrowding, inadequate water access, and shared tents lead to community attack rates exceeding 50%.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, child day-care centers, pre-school environments, pediatric transmission, play contact
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission frequently occurs in child day-care centers and preschool facilities, where interactive floor play, communal nap mats, and close tactile interactions facilitate rapid spread among infants and toddlers.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, remote island communities, South Pacific, Indigenous populations, hyperendemic prevalence
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies exhibits hyperendemic transmission in remote island communities (such as Fiji, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, and northern Australian Indigenous communities), where baseline prevalence often ranges from 20% to 50%.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, urban slum residence, informal settlements, high population density, tropical poverty
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies transmission is elevated by urban slum residence, where high population density, inadequate sanitation infrastructure, and limited access to healthcare perpetuate endemic transmission cycles in developing metropolises.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, primary infection incubation, 3 to 6 weeks, asymptomatic lag, delayed hypersensitivity
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Scabies exhibits a primary infection incubation period of 3 to 6 weeks (up to 4 to 6 weeks), during which the newly infested host remains completely asymptomatic while the female mite burrows and reproduces before delayed hypersensitivity develops.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, reinfestation incubation, 24 to 48 hours, accelerated onset, pre-existing sensitization
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Scabies exhibits an accelerated reinfestation incubation period of only 24 to 48 hours (hours to 2 days), where pre-existing memory T-cells mount an immediate, explosive inflammatory and pruritic response upon mite re-exposure.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, advanced HIV infection, CD4 lymphopenia, impaired cell-mediated immunity, Norwegian scabies
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets patients with advanced HIV infection and profound CD4+ T-cell depletion as a high-risk host group, where defective cell-mediated immunity fails to suppress parasite reproduction, leading to severe crusted Norwegian scabies.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, HTLV-1 coinfection, human T-cell leukemia virus, crusted scabies risk, cytokine imbalance
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets patients with HTLV-1 coinfection as an extraordinarily high-risk host population, where retrovirus-induced Th1/Th2 immune dysregulation strongly predisposes to refractory, life-threatening crusted Norwegian scabies.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, solid organ transplantation, calcineurin inhibitors, immunosuppressed host, crusted risk
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets solid organ transplantation recipients on maintenance immunosuppressive therapy (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, mycophenolate), predisposing them to hyperkeratotic crusted scabies presentations with high mite burdens.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, chronic corticosteroid therapy, systemic steroids, topical steroid misuse, suppressed pruritus
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets patients on chronic corticosteroid therapy as a high-risk host group, where suppression of epidermal inflammation eliminates host pruritic itching and grooming, permitting massive mite multiplication into crusted scabies.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, Down syndrome, trisomy 21, crusted scabies predisposition, immune alterations
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets individuals with Down syndrome as a recognized high-risk host demographic for crusted scabies, attributed to intrinsic abnormalities in cutaneous T-cell immunity, xerotic skin barrier changes, and altered sensory awareness.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, severe dementia, Alzheimer disease, cognitive impairment, lack of itch reporting
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets elderly patients with severe dementia as a high-risk host population, because impaired cognitive awareness prevents patients from recognizing or reporting pruritus, allowing unchecked mite proliferation and unnoticed institutional spread.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, bedridden debilitated patients, physical disability, stroke, immobility, grooming failure
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets bedridden debilitated patients with stroke, spinal injury, or severe neuromuscular weakness, who cannot physically scratch or groom themselves to mechanically dislodge mites, leading to extensive hyperkeratotic plaques.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pediatric age under 2, infants, neonates, immature skin barrier, severe disease
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets infants of pediatric age under two years as a uniquely susceptible host group with thin stratum corneum and immature cellular immunity, resulting in widespread acral and cephalic lesions and high secondary infection risk.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, elderly care residents, nursing home seniors, immunosenescence, outbreak epicenter
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets elderly care residents in assisted living facilities as a high-risk host demographic characterized by immunosenescence, fragile skin barriers, and frequent caregiver physical contact.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, household cluster itch, family contacts, nocturnal pruritus in family, epidemiologic anchor
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies is confirmed by exposure to household cluster itch, where history of identical severe nocturnal pruritus or typical papular rashes in close domestic contacts or bed partners provides a definitive epidemiologic anchor (2020 IACS Level B3).

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, total absence of pruritus, no itching, non-pruritic rash, immunocompetent host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by the total absence of pruritus in an alert, immunocompetent adolescent or adult host, as delayed-type hypersensitivity to mite proteins almost universally generates severe, distressing itch.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, adult facial involvement, facial and scalp rash, adult cephalic sparing, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by adult facial involvement and scalp eruption in an immunocompetent adult, because the adult Circle of Hebra strictly spares the head, neck, face, and scalp (unlike infantile scabies).

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, sparing of finger webs, clear web spaces, interdigital sparing, negative boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by complete sparing of finger webs and interdigital spaces in a patient presenting with generalized diffuse pruritic excoriations, which makes common scabies extraordinarily improbable.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, sparing of flexor wrists, clear volar wrists, absence of wrist lesions, negative boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by total sparing of flexor wrists and volar wrist skin creases in a patient with a widespread pruritic symmetrical eruption, strongly pointing toward alternative inflammatory dermatoses.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, high fever at onset, acute pyrexia, chills and rigors, absence of pyoderma
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated primary scabies is ruled out by high fever at onset (>38.5 C) accompanied by chills and rigors in the absence of obvious secondary bacterial pyoderma, cellulitis, or bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, systemic toxicity at onset, acute prostration, hemodynamic instability, non-superinfected host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated scabies is ruled out by acute systemic toxicity at onset, including hypotension, altered mental status, and prostration, which indicates invasive sepsis, toxic shock, or an alternative systemic infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, non-pruritic palmoplantar macules, copper-red spots, painless palms and soles, secondary syphilis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by non-pruritic palmoplantar macules, presenting as painless, copper-red or ham-colored macules on the palms and soles with generalized lymphadenopathy, which pathognomonically defines secondary syphilis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, isolated extensor plaque sparing, extensor knees and elbows, sparing flexures, psoriasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by isolated extensor plaque distribution with complete sparing of flexural creases, web spaces, and genitalia, which strongly indicates plaque psoriasis rather than an ectoparasitic infestation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, Auspitz sign positivity, punctate bleeding, silvery scale removal, plaque psoriasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Crusted scabies is ruled out by Auspitz sign positivity, where mechanical scraping of a thick silvery scale reveals pinpoint bleeding points from elongated dermal papillae without a single mite on microscopy, confirming psoriasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusive sun-exposed distribution, photo-distributed rash, sparing covered skin, photodermatitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by an exclusive sun-exposed distribution, where a pruritic eruption is strictly confined to the face, V of the neck, and dorsal forearms with complete sparing of clothed areas, indicating photodermatosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, pure mucosal ulceration, oral aphthae, genital mucous erosions, non-epidermal involvement
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by pure mucosal ulceration involving oral or genital mucous membranes without epidermal burrows, papules, or web-space lesions, as Sarcoptes mites cannot burrow into non-cornified mucous membranes.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, targetoid iris lesions, concentric rings, three-zone targets, erythema multiforme
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by classic targetoid iris lesions consisting of three concentric concentric color zones with central dusky purpura, which definitively characterizes erythema multiforme.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, flaccid bullae with Nikolsky, positive Nikolsky sign, intraepidermal acantholysis, pemphigus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by flaccid bullae with positive Nikolsky sign (epidermal sheet detachment upon lateral mechanical pressure), indicating intraepidermal acantholytic disease such as pemphigus vulgaris rather than scabies.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rapid day-one rash resolution, evanescent lesions, resolution under 24 hours, allergic urticaria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Active scabies is ruled out by rapid day-one rash resolution, where individual pruritic lesions spontaneously resolve completely within 24 hours without scabicidal therapy, identifying evanescent acute urticaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lack of household itch, chronic solitary pruritus, zero transmission to bed partner, chronic pruritus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by lack of household itch in the context of chronic severe nocturnal pruritus persisting for more than 1 to 2 years with zero transmission to sleeping partners or family members.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal serum IgE Norwegian, normal IgE, normal eosinophils, pseudo-crusted lesion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Suspected crusted (Norwegian) scabies is ruled out by normal serum IgE and normal eosinophil counts in a patient with extensive psoriasiform hyperkeratotic crusts, as true crusted scabies drives massive IgE and eosinophil surges.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, ceftriaxone monotherapy response, cephalosporin clearance, antibiotic rash cure, bacterial mimic
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Primary scabies is ruled out by prompt cure on ceftriaxone monotherapy, where the entire pruritic eruption clears completely on standard cephalosporins without topical or oral scabicides, proving an exclusive bacterial etiology.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, burrow and mite absence, negative serial scrapings, negative dermoscopy, high pretest certainty
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by definitive burrow and mite absence on serial high-resolution videodermoscopy and multiple deep mineral oil scrapings performed by expert dermatologists across multiple typical anatomical sites.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, wheals resolving under 24h, transient edematous plaques, evanescent hives, urticaria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by transient pruritic edematous wheals resolving under 24 hours without residual epidermal scaling or excoriations, characteristic of common urticaria rather than an intraepidermal mite infestation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusive scalp folliculitis, follicular pustules, head-only lesions, bacterial folliculitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by exclusive scalp folliculitis where inflammatory pustules are confined strictly to hair follicles on the scalp and face with zero lesions on the body, wrists, or genitalia in an adult.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, unilateral dermatomal vesicles, grouped blisters, single dermatome, herpes zoster
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by unilateral dermatomal vesicles presenting as painful grouped fluid-filled blisters strictly confined within a single sensory dermatome respecting the midline, definitively diagnostic of herpes zoster.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, petechial non-blanching purpura, palpable purpura, leukocytoclastic vasculitis, extravasation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by widespread petechial non-blanching purpura and palpable purpuric papules on dependent lower extremities, indicating cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis rather than ectoparasitosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, atopic dermatitis, eczema, look-alike, flexural crease distribution, lack of burrows
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from atopic dermatitis because atopic dermatitis primarily involves flexural creases (antecubital and popliteal fossae), face, and neck with chronic personal or family atopic diathesis, whereas scabies features pathognomonic intraepidermal burrows, interdigital web lesions, pruritic male genital nodules, and rapid transmission to household contacts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, bullous pemphigoid, autoimmune blistering, look-alike, tense subepidermal bullae, DIF linear IgG
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from bullous pemphigoid because bullous pemphigoid produces tense, large subepidermal bullae on normal or erythematous skin with linear IgG and C3 deposition along the dermal-epidermal junction on direct immunofluorescence and elevated anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies, whereas bullous scabies reveals intraepidermal burrows, delta-wing sign on dermoscopy, and mites on mineral oil scraping.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, insect bites, arthropod bites, flea bites, breakfast lunch dinner pattern, exposed extremities
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from insect bites (arthropod assault) because insect bites typically present with grouped, pruritic wheals or papules with a central punctum distributed in asymmetric clusters on exposed limbs (the 'breakfast, lunch, and dinner' sign), lacking intraepidermal burrows, web space involvement, or genital nodules.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, plaque psoriasis, psoriasis vulgaris, look-alike, extensor plaques, Auspitz sign, Norwegian mimic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies (specifically crusted Norwegian scabies) is differentiated from plaque psoriasis because psoriasis features well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery micaceous scales on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees), positive Auspitz sign, nail pitting, and zero mites on skin scraping, whereas crusted scabies scrapings yield millions of living mites, eggs, and scybala.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, secondary syphilis, Treponema pallidum, look-alike, non-pruritic macules, condyloma lata
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from secondary syphilis because secondary syphilis presents with painless, non-pruritic copper-colored macules on the palms and soles, generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy, condyloma lata, mucosal patches, and reactive treponemal serology (RPR/VDRL and TPPA), whereas scabies presents with severe nocturnal itch, linear burrows, and negative treponemal tests.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, papular urticaria, pediatric hypersensitivity, look-alike, recurrent wheals, absence of burrows
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from papular urticaria because papular urticaria represents a chronic pediatric hypersensitivity to sporadic insect stings manifesting as recurrent crops of evanescent pruritic wheals and excoriated central papules without intraepidermal burrows, interdigital localization, or simultaneous infestation of family co-habitants.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, folliculitis, bacterial folliculitis, look-alike, hair-pierced pustules, absence of tunnels
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from bacterial folliculitis because folliculitis lesions are strictly centered around hair follicles, each pierced by a central hair shaft, distributed on friction-bearing hairy skin (thighs, buttocks, beard) without linear burrows or interdigital web tracks.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, contact dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, look-alike, geometric pattern, exposure history
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from allergic or irritant contact dermatitis because contact dermatitis lesions are sharply demarcated and correspond geometrically to exogenous chemical or allergen contact boundaries (e.g., waistband elastic, nickel snaps, poison ivy lines) and completely lack linear burrows, male genital nodules, or contagion to bed partners.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff, look-alike, greasy scales, sebaceous area predilection
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from seborrheic dermatitis because seborrheic dermatitis produces greasy, yellowish scales overlying mild erythema confined strictly to sebum-rich regions (scalp, nasolabial folds, eyebrows, central chest) with minimal itch, whereas classical adult scabies strictly spares the face and scalp.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Darier disease, keratosis follicularis, look-alike, autosomal dominant, greasy warty papules
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies (specifically crusted Norwegian scabies) is differentiated from Darier disease because Darier disease (keratosis follicularis) is an autosomal dominant genodermatosis presenting with firm, greasy, hyperkeratotic, warty papules in seborrheic distributions, distinctive nail V-nicks, corps ronds and grains on biopsy, and absence of parasites.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, dermatitis herpetiformis, celiac-associated, look-alike, extensor grouped vesicles, granular IgA
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from dermatitis herpetiformis because dermatitis herpetiformis produces intensely pruritic grouped polymorphous papulovesicles symmetrically distributed over extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, buttocks, scalp), strongly associates with gluten-sensitive enteropathy, and shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae on direct immunofluorescence.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, pityriasis rosea, herald patch, look-alike, Christmas tree pattern, Langer lines
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from pityriasis rosea because pityriasis rosea begins with an initial solitary 'herald patch' followed by an eruption of oval, salmon-colored macules with collarette scaling oriented along skin cleavage lines ('Christmas-tree distribution'), sparing the hands, feet, and genitalia, and resolving spontaneously in 6 to 8 weeks.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, cutaneous larva migrans, hookworm, look-alike, rapid advancing tracks, sandy soil exposure
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from cutaneous larva migrans (creeping eruption) because larva migrans causes rapidly advancing, intensely erythematous, tortuous serpiginous tracks progressing 1 to 2 cm daily, typically on the feet or buttocks following tropical sandy soil contact, whereas scabies burrows progress much slower (0.5 to 5 mm/day), cluster in web spaces and flexures, and spread from person to person.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, delusional parasitosis, Ekbom syndrome, look-alike, matchbox sign, lack of true lesions
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from delusional parasitosis (Ekbom syndrome) because delusional parasitosis presents with a fixed false belief of insect or mite infestation in the complete absence of objective burrows, papules, or microscopic findings, frequently accompanied by the 'matchbox sign' where patients present containers of epidermal lint, fibers, or dried skin flakes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, dyshidrotic eczema, pompholyx, look-alike, tapioca-like vesicles, lateral fingers
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from dyshidrotic eczema (pompholyx) because dyshidrotic eczema produces deep-seated, intensely pruritic 'tapioca-like' microvesicles restricted strictly to the lateral aspects of fingers, palms, and soles without linear burrows, male genital lesions, or contagious spread to family contacts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, lichen planus, 6 Ps, look-alike, Wickham striae, mucosal lacy plaques, volar wrists
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from lichen planus because lichen planus presents with the classic '6 Ps' (pruritic, planar, polygonal, purple, papules, and plaques) exhibiting fine reticular surface white lines (Wickham striae) on volar wrists and lacy oral mucosal plaques, completely lacking intraepidermal burrow tracks or mites.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, varicella zoster virus, chickenpox, look-alike, dewdrops on rose petal, acute fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from varicella zoster virus (chickenpox) because varicella presents acutely with fever, malaise, and a rapid cephalocaudal progression of polymorphic pruritic vesicles in various stages ('dewdrops on a rose petal') resolving over 7 to 10 days with positive viral PCR or Tzanck smear, whereas scabies is an unremitting afebrile ectoparasitosis lacking systemic viremia.
